2400: second person singular imperative middle voice of εἴδω; used as imperative lo!; --behold, lo, see.
2401: of Hebrew origin (אֱדֹם); Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine:--Idumæa.
2402: a strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat); perspiration:--sweat.
2403: of Hebrew origin (אִיזֶבֶל); Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher):--Jezabel.
2404: from ἱερός and πόλις; holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor:--Hierapolis.
2405: from ἱερατεύω; priestliness, i.e. the sacerdotal function:--office of the priesthood, priest's office.
2406: from ἱερατεύω; the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively):--priesthood.
2407: prolongation from ἱερεύς; to be a priest, i.e. perform his functions:--execute the priest's office.
2408: of Hebrew origin (יִרְמְיָה); Hieremias (i.e. Jermijah), an Israelite:--Jeremiah.
2409: from ἱερός; a priest (literally or figuratively):--(high) priest.
2410: of Hebrew origin (יְרִיחוֹ); Jericho, a place in Palestine:--Jericho.
2411: neuter of ἱερός; a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas ναός denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem or elsewhere):--temple.
2412: from ἱερός and the same as πρέπω; reverent:--as becometh holiness.
2414: of Hebrew origin (יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם); Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol of Palestine:--Jerusalem. Compare Ἱερουσαλήμ.
2415: from Ἱεροσόλυμα; a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma:--of Jerusalem.
2416: from ἱερόσυλος; to be a temple-robber (figuratively):--commit sacrilege.
2417: from ἱερόν and συλάω; a temple-despoiler:--robber of churches.
2418: from a compound of ἱερόν and the base of ἔργον; to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively):--minister.
2419: of Hebrew origin (יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם); Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine:--Jerusalem. Compare Ἱεροσόλυμα.
2420: from ἱερός; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office:--priesthood.
2421: of Hebrew origin (יִשַׁי); Jessæ (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite:--Jesse.
2422: of Hebrew origin (יִפְתָּח); Jephthaë (i.e. Jiphtach), an Israelite:--Jephthah.
2423: of Hebrew origin (יְכׇנְיָה); Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an Israelite:--Jechonias.
2424: of Hebrew origin (יְהוֹשׁוּעַ); Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites:--Jesus.
2425: from ( or , akin to ἥκω) (to arrive); competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character):--able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy.
2427: from ἱκανός; to enable, i.e. qualify:--make able (meet).
2428: from a derivative of the base of ἱκανός (through the idea of approaching for a favor); intreaty:--supplication.
2430: perhaps from εἰκών; image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor:--Iconium.
2431: from the same as ἵλεως; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing:--cheerful.
2433: middle voice from the same as ἵλεως; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious:--be merciful, make reconciliation for.
2435: neuter of a derivative of ἱλάσκομαι; an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple):--mercyseat, propitiation.
2436: perhaps from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι; cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it:--be it far, merciful.
2437: neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation; (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe:--Illyricum.
2438: perhaps from the same as ἅμα; a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge):--latchet, thong.
2440: neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on); a dress (inner or outer):--apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture.
2441: from ἱματίζω; clothing:--apparel (X -led), array, raiment, vesture.
2442: middle voice from (a yearning; of uncertain affinity); to long for:--be affectionately desirous.
2443: probably from the same as the former part of ἑαυτοῦ (through the demonstrative idea; compare ὁ); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result):--albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to. Compare ἵνα μή.
2444: from ἵνα and τίς; for what reason ?, i.e. why?:--wherefore, why.
2445: of Hebrew origin (יָפוֹ); Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine:--Joppa.
2446: of Hebrew origin (יַרְדֵּן); the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of Palestine:--Jordan.
2447: perhaps from (to go) or (to send); rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents):--poison, rust.
2448: of Hebrew origin (יְהוּדָה or perhaps יֻטָּה); Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine:--Judah.
2449: feminine of Ἰουδαῖος (with γῆ implied); the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa), a region of Palestine:--Judæa.
2450: from Ἰουδαῖος; to become a Judæan, i.e. "Judaize":--live as the Jews.
2451: from Ἰουδαῖος; Judaïc, i.e. resembling a Judæan:--Jewish.
2452: adverb from Ἰουδαϊκός; Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan:--as do the Jews.
2453: from Ἰουδά (in the sense of Ἰούδας as a country); Judæan, i.e. belonging to Jehudah:--Jew(-ess), of Judæa.
2454: from Ἰουδαΐζω; "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages:--Jews' religion.
2455: of Hebrew origin (יְהוּדָה); Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region:--Juda(-h, -s); Jude.
2456: feminine of the same as Ἰούλιος; Julia, a Christian woman:--Julia.
2457: of Latin origin; Julius, a centurion:--Julius.
2458: of Latin origin; Junias, a Christian:--Junias.
2459: of Latin origin ("just"); Justus, the name of three Christian:--Justus.
2460: from ἵππος; an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps:--horseman.
2461: neuter of a derivative of ἵππος; the cavalry force:--horse(-men).
2463: perhaps from ἐρέω (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities); a rainbow ("iris"):--rainbow.
2464: of Hebrew origin (יִצְחָק); Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham:--Isaac.
2465: from ἴσος and ἄγγελος; like an angel, i.e. angelic:--equal unto the angels.
2466: of Hebrew origin (יִשָּׂשכָר); Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant):--Issachar.
2467: assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of εἴδω; to know:--know.
2468: second person imperative present of εἰμί; be thou:--+ agree, be, X give thyself wholly to.
2469: of Hebrew origin (probably אִישׁ and קִרְיָא); inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor:--Iscariot.
2470: probably from εἴδω (through the idea of seeming); similar (in amount and kind):--+ agree, as much, equal, like.
2472: from ἴσος and τιμή; of equal value or honor:--like precious.
2473: from ἴσος and ψυχή; of similar spirit:--likeminded.
2474: of Hebrew origin (יִשְׂרָאֵל); Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively):--Israel.
2475: from Ἰσραήλ; an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively):--Israelite.
2476: a prolonged form of a primary (of the same meaning, and used for it in certain tenses); to stand (transitively or intransitively), used in various applications (literally or figuratively):--abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish, hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up). Compare τίθημι.
2477: from a derivative of εἴδω; to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview):--see.
2478: from ἰσχύς; forcible (literally or figuratively):--boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant.
2479: from a derivative of (force; compare , a form of ἔχω); forcefulness (literally or figuratively):--ability, might(-ily), power, strength.
2480: from ἰσχύς; to have (or exercise) force (literally or figuratively):--be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might, prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work.
2481: adverb from ἴσος; likely, i.e. perhaps:--it may be.
2482: probably of foreign origin; Italia, a region of Europe:--Italy.
2483: from Ἰταλία; Italic, i.e. belonging to Italia:--Italian.
2484: of Hebrew origin (יְטוּר); Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine:--Ituræa.
2485: diminutive from ἰχθύς; a petty fish:--little (small) fish.
2487: from (to arrive; compare ἥκω); a track (figuratively):--step.
2488: of Hebrew origin (יוֹתָם); Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an Israelite:--Joatham.
2489: feminine of the same as Ἰωάννης; Joanna, a Christian:--Joanna.
2490: a form of Ἰωάννης; Joannas, an Israelite:--Joannas.
2491: of Hebrew origin (יוֹחָנָן); Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites:--John.
2492: of Hebrew origin (אִיּוֹב); Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch:--Job.
2493: of Hebrew origin (יוֹאֵל); Joel, an Israelite:--Joel.
2494: probably for Ἰωάννης or Ἰωνᾶς; Jonan, an Israelite:--Jonan.
2495: of Hebrew origin (יוֹנָה); Jonas (i.e. Jonah), the name of two Israelites:--Jonas.
2496: of Hebrew origin (יוֹרָם); Joram, an Israelite:--Joram.
2497: perhaps for Ἰωράμ; Jorim, an Israelite:--Jorim.
2498: of Hebrew origin (יְהוֹשָׁפָט); Josaphat (i.e. Jehoshaphat), an Israelite:--Josaphat.
2499: genitive case of Ἰωσῆς; Jose, an Israelite:--Jose.
